newsitem.title: USA: Kiwi Int'l gets extension on funding deadline.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi Int'l gets extension on funding deadline.

text.p: Federal bankruptcy judge Rosemary Gambardella extended until November 27 Kiwi International Air Lines's deadline to finalize its $5 million financing deal with ISBRE Holding Co.
Kiwi appeared in bankruptcy court on Friday to present a debtor-in-possession financing plan, but the deadline was extended because ISBRE was not able to come up with the financing.
"Circumstances developed and ISBRE is not in the position to come up with the funds today, but they assure me they'll have the money by next week," said Kiwi attorney Howard Greenberg.
As a "good faith effort," ISBRE will give Kiwi $60,000 in the interim to pay some insurance bills, Greenberg said.
Linden, N.J.-based ISBRE owns American Helicopters.
Kiwi suspended operations on October 15, after filing for Chapter 11 bankruptcy on September 30 under a $40 million debt load.
